neighbours.label: the word just before an expected 'look' or 'glance' noun: 'take a closer [look]', 'cast a quick [glance]' (also Russian бросил быстрый [взгляд], French jeter un [coup d'oeil]); the + pole fires on the word 'look' itself
fire: In this chapter we will take a closer look at how the engine is cooled.
The guard cast a quick glance over his shoulder and kept walking.
Come round on Sunday and have a closer look at the garden before you decide.
She stole a quick glance at her phone under the table.
Scientists are now taking a closer look at the samples from the cave.
He shot a quick glance toward the exit as the lights went down.
It is worth taking a closer look at the small print in the contract.
The waiter threw a quick glance at the empty glasses and came over.
quiet: In this chapter we will take a short walk through how the engine is cooled.
The guard cast a long shadow over the path and kept walking.
Come round on Sunday and have a hot meal in the garden before you decide.
She sent a short message from her phone under the table.
Scientists are now taking a large share of the samples from the cave.
He fired a single shot toward the exit as the lights went down.
It is worth taking a deep breath before you sign the contract.
The waiter threw a clean cloth over the empty table and came over.

notes: Card: peaks ' Gl' (at a Gl|ance) x6, ' take' x4, ' un', ' a', and Russian adjective endings before взгляд; the + direction suppresses look/glance/gaze, so this pole promotes them. Probes: 'take a closer look' 0.48 (peak ' closer'), 'cast a quick glance' 0.38 (peak ' quick'); 'take a short break' 0.15, 'threw a heavy stone' 0.12, 'at a glance' 0.08 (single-token 'glance'), 'gave her a long look' 0.03.
